title: 47th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened with 47 members present. The Speaker announced a Finance Minister letter on how 2025 budget block grants to councils are calculated, which went to the Budget Review Committee. The Minister of Education then answered questions from 12 members about school projects, payment delays, the CHSC closure and staffing. After that, members debated a government bill to amend the Penal Code's unexplained-wealth offence. After a break, the Majlis approved Fathimath Ameeza as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation, 64 votes to 0.

items.title: Attendance of members
items.outcome: 47 present, 6 on leave, 5 on official travel

items.title: Approval of minutes of sittings 2024/39 to 2024/42
Speaker's announcement: Finance Minister's letter on 2025 budget block grants to councils
items.outcome: letter sent to the Budget Review Committee

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Education
items.outcome: 12 members questioned the Minister; an urgent matter from North Galolhu was ruled not to meet Rule 197(a)

items.title: Debate on the bill amending the Penal Code (Law 9/2014) on unexplained wealth
items.outcome: debated by 5 members; no vote recorded in these minutes

items.title: Economic Committee report on nominees for Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation
items.outcome: report presented; no member asked to debate it

speakers.name: Dr. Ismail Shafeeu
positions: As Education Minister, said a 280 million rufiyaa backlog of unpaid contractor bills was a main cause of stalled school projects.
Said the Dharumavantha school hall plan was not budgeted for 2024 and the jail site would need to be vacated first.
Said he would check complaints about principals and staff fairly before acting, and denied any pay-framework change for teachers.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked about the hall planned at Dharumavantha School beside the jail, and questioned the Minister's unanswered letter.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill but urged careful rules and a fair justice system so it is not used for political ends.
Thanked the Economic Committee chair and members for their report.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when stalled classroom work at Nekurandhoo school and the Kumundhoo school boundary wall will start.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Raised parents' concern about a Baa Atoll school run by a larger school and teaching students online.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked about progress on Addu school projects including a multipurpose hall and the Arabiyya School works.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked when Velidhoo school's multipurpose hall starts and when the stalled classroom work will finish.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked how closing CHSC in Malé affected students and parents, and whether the benefits outweighed the hardship.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked why budgeted Keyodhoo school works have not started and whether families sending children away will get support.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when Kulhudhuffushi school classroom and building works will finish, citing over 3,000 pupils and crowding.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked about a school library and science lab, Grade 10 pupils studying at home, and Grade 8 exam changes.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked whether complaints that some principals treat pupils differently were noticed and acted on.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked how the Ministry will fix delays in school projects caused by budget and payment problems.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked why the school breakfast programme stopped and how much was owed to its providers.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the unexplained-wealth amendment, recounting the law's history and saying it can help recover wrongly gained assets.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the bill but questioned the definition of a state employee and urged broader coverage of unlawful wealth.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Argued anti-corruption bodies had failed to act, and urged strict enforcement including cases involving members.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the 2014 law was seldom applied, and wanted it to cover all officials and citizens, not only state employees.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report recommending Fathimath Ameeza and Asma Shafeeq, both qualified and above 75 percent.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2024/39 to 2024/42 were accepted.
The Finance Minister's letter on 2025 budget block grants was sent to the Budget Review Committee.
The Speaker ruled the urgent matter from the North Galolhu member did not meet Rule 197(a), so no vote on debating it was held.
Fathimath Ameeza was approved as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation by 64 votes to 0.
The next sitting was set for 12 November 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Approval of Fathimath Ameeza as Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation
